# useIntersecting

Determine whether the target element intersects the viewport (or the specified `root`).

## API

```ts
function useIntersecting(
  target: Element | React.RefObject<Element | null>,
  options?: {
    root?: Element | Document | React.RefObject<Element | Document | null>;
    rootMargin?: string;
    threshold?: number | number[];
  },
): boolean;
```

Parameters:

- **`target`:** A DOM element to observe, or a ref object that references it.
- **`options`:** See [IntersectionObserver](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/IntersectionObserver/IntersectionObserver) options.

Results:

- A boolean indicating whether the target is intersecting with the root.

## Notes

- Returns `false` in non-browser environments.
- Resets to `false` when the target element becomes invalid.

## Example

The following example scrolls a container and highlights the target when it is fully visible.

```tsx
import { useRef } from "react";
import { useIntersecting } from "@lilib/hooks";

function Example() {
  const rootRef = useRef(null);
  const targetRef = useRef(null);

  const intersecting = useIntersecting(targetRef, {
    root: rootRef,
    threshold: 1,
  });

  return (
    <div ref={rootRef} style={{ height: 200, overflow: "auto" }}>
      <div
        ref={targetRef}
        style={{
          height: 100,
          marginTop: 150,
          marginBottom: 150,
          backgroundColor: intersecting ? "orange" : "transparent",
        }}
      >
        {intersecting ? "Complete intersection" : "Incomplete intersection"}
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}

export default Example;
```

---

# useClickOutside

Trigger a callback when a click happens outside the target area.

## API

```ts
function useClickOutside<E extends Event = Event>(
  target: Node | React.RefObject<Node | null> | (Node | React.RefObject<Node | null>)[],
  listener: (event: E) => void,
  options?: {
    container?: Element | React.RefObject<Element | null>;
    eventName?: string | string[];
  },
): void;
```

Parameters:

- **`target`:** The target area: a single element or element ref, or an array of them. The listener fires when a click happens outside all of these targets. It only fires when at least one target element is valid; all-invalid targets are treated as not ready.
- **`listener`:** The callback invoked when a click happens outside the target area.
- **`options`:** Options object.
  - **`options.container`:** The element (or its ref) that receives the event listener. Default is `document`.
  - **`options.eventName`:** Event name or names. Default is `"mousedown"`.

## Notes

- The default event is `mousedown`, not `click`: interactions that only produce a `click` event will not trigger the listener. Pass `eventName: ["mousedown", "click"]` if needed.
- Taps on touch devices do not always produce a `mousedown` event; add `"touchstart"` or `"pointerdown"` to `eventName` to support them.
- The `container` option receives the event listener, so it must be an ancestor of the click source for the event to bubble to it.

## Example

The following example counts clicks outside the button (typical for closing dropdowns).

```tsx
import { useRef, useState } from "react";
import { useClickOutside } from "@lilib/hooks";

function Example() {
  const buttonRef = useRef(null);
  const [count, setCount] = useState(0);

  useClickOutside(buttonRef, () => {
    setCount(count + 1);
  });

  return (
    <>
      <button ref={buttonRef}>Click outside</button> Count: {count}
    </>
  );
}

export default Example;
```

---

# useEventListener

Set up an event listener on the target.

## API

```ts
function useEventListener<T extends EventTarget = EventTarget, E extends Event = Event>(
  target: T | React.RefObject<T | null>,
  eventName: string,
  listener: (event: E) => void,
  options?: boolean | { capture?: boolean; once?: boolean; passive?: boolean },
): void;
```

Parameters:

- **`target`:** An event target, or a ref object that references an event target (or `null`).
- **`eventName`:** Event name.
- **`listener`:** Listener function.
- **`options`:** Similar to the third parameter of the [`addEventListener`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/EventTarget/addEventListener) function, but only the `capture`, `once` and `passive` options are used.

## Notes

- When `target` is a ref, the listener is attached when the referenced node appears and re-attached when it changes; nothing happens while it is `null`.
- The `listener` is always the latest render's function, so it never reads stale closures.

## Example

The following example counts clicks on a button.

```tsx
import { useRef, useState } from "react";
import { useEventListener } from "@lilib/hooks";

function Example() {
  const buttonRef = useRef<HTMLButtonElement>(null);
  const [count, setCount] = useState(0);

  useEventListener(buttonRef, "click", () => {
    setCount((count) => count + 1);
  });

  return (
    <>
      <button ref={buttonRef}>Click</button> Count: {count}
    </>
  );
}

export default Example;
```

---

# useResizeObserver

Observe an element's size changes.

## API

```ts
function useResizeObserver(
  target: Element | React.RefObject<Element | null>,
  listener: (entries: ResizeObserverEntry[]) => void,
): void;
```

Parameters:

- **`target`:** A DOM element to observe, or a ref object that references it.
- **`listener`:** Listener function.

## Notes

- The `resize-observer-polyfill` is always used (it does not delegate to the native implementation); mind the performance cost for high-frequency resizes.
- The listener attaches once the target element is mounted; a ref that is still `null` is fine.

## Example

The following example counts resize events when the element size changes.

```tsx
import { useRef, useState } from "react";
import { useResizeObserver } from "@lilib/hooks";

function Example() {
  const [wide, setWide] = useState(false);
  const [count, setCount] = useState(0);
  const containerRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);

  useResizeObserver(containerRef, () => {
    setCount((count) => count + 1);
  });

  return (
    <>
      <div>
        <button onClick={() => setWide((wide) => !wide)}>Toggle size</button>
      </div>
      <div
        ref={containerRef}
        style={{
          padding: 16,
          width: wide ? "100%" : "50%",
          backgroundColor: "rgba(255, 165, 0, 0.3)",
        }}
      >
        Resized times: {count}
      </div>
    </>
  );
}

export default Example;
```

---

# useMutationObserver

Observe changes to a DOM node, such as inserted or removed child nodes and changed attributes.

## API

```ts
function useMutationObserver(
  target: Node | React.RefObject<Node | null>,
  listener: (records: MutationRecord[]) => void,
  options?: MutationObserverInit,
): void;
```

Parameters:

- **`target`:** A DOM node to observe, or a ref object that references it.
- **`listener`:** Listener function invoked with the mutation records.
- **`options`:** See [MutationObserver](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/MutationObserver/observe) options. Omitted, it defaults to `{ childList: true, attributes: true, characterData: true }`; when provided, it replaces the defaults instead of merging with them.

## Notes

- When `options` is provided, it replaces the defaults instead of merging with them, so at least one of `childList`, `attributes` and `characterData` must end up enabled, otherwise `observe` throws a `TypeError`.
- `attributeFilter` is compared by content, so inline arrays do not recreate the observer on every render.

## Example

The following example reports the type of the latest mutation of a text node.

```tsx
import { useRef, useState } from "react";
import { useMutationObserver } from "@lilib/hooks";

function Example() {
  const [content, setContent] = useState("Hello");
  const [lastMutation, setLastMutation] = useState("None");
  const containerRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);

  useMutationObserver(
    containerRef,
    (records) => {
      const record = records[0];
      setLastMutation(record ? record.type : "None");
    },
    { childList: true, characterData: true, subtree: true },
  );

  return (
    <>
      <div>
        <button onClick={() => setContent((content) => (content === "Hello" ? "World" : "Hello"))}>
          Change text
        </button>
      </div>
      <div
        ref={containerRef}
        style={{
          padding: 16,
          backgroundColor: "rgba(255, 165, 0, 0.3)",
        }}
      >
        {content}
      </div>
      <div>Last mutation: {lastMutation}</div>
    </>
  );
}

export default Example;
```

---

# useIntersectionObserver

Observe when an element's intersection with another element or the viewport changes.

## API

```ts
function useIntersectionObserver(
  target: Element | React.RefObject<Element | null>,
  listener: (entries: IntersectionObserverEntry[]) => void,
  options?: {
    root?: Element | Document | React.RefObject<Element | Document | null>;
    rootMargin?: string;
    threshold?: number | number[];
  },
): void;
```

Parameters:

- **`target`:** A DOM element to observe, or a ref object that references it.
- **`listener`:** Listener function.
- **`options`:** See [IntersectionObserver](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/IntersectionObserver/IntersectionObserver) options.

## Notes

- Observes through a layout effect: the observer is created before the browser paints.
- The observer attaches once the target element is mounted; a ref that is still `null` is fine.
- An array `threshold` is compared by content, so inline arrays do not recreate the observer on every render.

## Example

The following example scrolls a container and highlights the target when it is fully visible.

```tsx
import { useRef, useState } from "react";
import { useIntersectionObserver } from "@lilib/hooks";

function Example() {
  const [intersecting, setIntersecting] = useState(false);
  const rootRef = useRef(null);
  const targetRef = useRef(null);

  useIntersectionObserver(
    targetRef,
    (entries) => {
      if (entries && entries[0] && entries[0].isIntersecting) {
        setIntersecting(true);
      } else {
        setIntersecting(false);
      }
    },
    { root: rootRef, threshold: 1 },
  );

  return (
    <div
      ref={rootRef}
      style={{
        height: 200,
        overflow: "auto",
      }}
    >
      <div
        ref={targetRef}
        style={{
          height: 100,
          marginTop: 150,
          marginBottom: 150,
          backgroundColor: intersecting ? "orange" : "transparent",
        }}
      >
        {intersecting ? "Complete intersection" : "Incomplete intersection"}
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}

export default Example;
```

---

# useCookie

This hook uses [js-cookie](https://github.com/js-cookie/js-cookie) as the parser. You can use this hook to get, set and/or remove cookies.

## API

```ts
interface UseCookieOptions {
  defaultValue?: string;
  polling?: boolean;
  pollingInterval?: number;
  validate?: (value: string) => boolean;
}

function useCookie(
  name: string,
  options: UseCookieOptions & { defaultValue: string },
): [
  value: string,
  setCookie: (
    newValue: string | undefined | ((prevValue: string) => string | undefined),
    attributes?: CookieAttributes,
  ) => void,
];

function useCookie(
  name: string,
  options?: UseCookieOptions,
): [
  value: string | undefined,
  setCookie: (
    newValue: string | undefined | ((prevValue: string | undefined) => string | undefined),
    attributes?: CookieAttributes,
  ) => void,
];

interface CookieAttributes {
  path?: string;
  domain?: string;
  secure?: boolean;
  expires?: number | Date;
  sameSite?: "strict" | "Strict" | "lax" | "Lax" | "none" | "None";
}
```

Parameters:

- **`name`:** Cookie name.
- **`options`:** Options object.
  - **`options.defaultValue`:** Default value. It will be returned when the specified cookie doesn't exist. When set, the returned `value` type no longer includes `undefined`.
  - **`options.polling`:** Whether to poll for cookie changes. Default is `false`.
  - **`options.pollingInterval`:** Polling interval time, in milliseconds. Default is `100`.
  - **`options.validate`:** Validate the value got from the cookie. If this function returns `false`, the `defaultValue` will be used.

Results:

- **`value`:** Cookie value.
- **`setCookie`:** A function that can set or remove the named cookie. It accepts two params:
  - **`newValue`:** The new cookie value. If it is `undefined` or a function that returns `undefined`, the named cookie will be cleared, and the `options.defaultValue` will be returned as `value`.
  - **`attributes`:** Cookie attributes. See [js-cookie attributes](https://github.com/js-cookie/js-cookie#cookie-attributes).

## Notes

- **Important**: Removing a cookie requires the same `attributes` as when it was set (especially `path` and `domain`); otherwise the removal silently fails.
- Cookie changes made elsewhere (server responses, other scripts) are not pushed to the hook; enable `polling: true` to detect them.
- Values are strings — no serialization is applied. Use `JSON.stringify` together with `validate` for structured data.
- Returns `defaultValue` in non-browser environments. The `value` starts with `defaultValue` on the first render and is synchronized with the cookie right after mounting (before the browser paints), so server-rendered and client-hydrated output stay consistent.

## Example

The following example sets and removes a cookie; open this page in another tab to see polling keep the values in sync.

```tsx
import { useCookie } from "@lilib/hooks";

function Example() {
  const [value, setCookie] = useCookie("name", {
    polling: true,
    defaultValue: "default value",
  });

  return (
    <>
      <div>
        <button onClick={() => setCookie(Math.random().toString())}>Set random cookie</button>{" "}
        <button onClick={() => setCookie(undefined)}>Remove</button>
      </div>
      <div>Cookie value: {value}</div>
    </>
  );
}

export default Example;
```

---

# useLocalStorage

Get, set and/or remove `localStorage`.

## API

```ts
interface UseStorageOptions<T> {
  defaultValue?: T;
  polling?: boolean;
  pollingInterval?: number;
  compare?: (x: any, y: any) => boolean;
  validate?: (value: any) => boolean;
  serialize?: (value: T) => string;
  deserialize?: (raw: string) => T;
}

function useLocalStorage<T>(
  key: string,
  options: UseStorageOptions<T> & { defaultValue: T },
): [
  value: T,
  setLocalStorage: (newValue: T | undefined | ((prevValue: T) => T | undefined)) => void,
];

function useLocalStorage<T>(
  key: string,
  options?: UseStorageOptions<T>,
): [
  value: T | undefined,
  setLocalStorage: (
    newValue: T | undefined | ((prevValue: T | undefined) => T | undefined),
  ) => void,
];
```

Parameters:

- **`key`:** `localStorage` key.
- **`options`:** Options object.
  - **`options.defaultValue`:** Default value. When set, the returned `value` type no longer includes `undefined`.
  - **`options.polling`:** Whether to poll for storage changes. Default is `false`.
  - **`options.pollingInterval`:** Polling interval time, in milliseconds. Default is `100`.
  - **`options.compare`:** A function to determine whether the new and old values are equal. Defaults to deep comparison.
  - **`options.validate`:** Validate the value got from `localStorage` which is deserialized by the `deserialize` function. If this function returns `false`, the `defaultValue` will be used.
  - **`options.serialize`:** Serialization function. Default is `JSON.stringify`.
  - **`options.deserialize`:** Deserialization function. Default is `JSON.parse`.

Results:

- **`value`:** The value parsed by the deserialization function.
- **`setLocalStorage`:** Set `localStorage`. The `newValue` can also be a function that returns the new value. If it is `undefined`, the entry will be removed and the `defaultValue` will be returned.

## Notes

- **Important**: The `storage` event fires only in other tabs/windows — it never fires in the document that made the change. Components in the same page only stay in sync when they use the same hook instance, or with `polling: true`.
- The default serialization is `JSON.stringify`/`JSON.parse`: `Date` becomes a string, `NaN` and `Infinity` become `null`, `Map`/`Set`/circular references are lost, and `undefined` array items become `null`. Use `serialize`/`deserialize` for custom types.
- In private-browsing or restricted environments, accessing `localStorage` may throw; the hook then falls back to in-memory state and writes are not persisted.
- Returns `defaultValue` in non-browser environments. The `value` starts with `defaultValue` on the first render and is synchronized with the stored value right after mounting (before the browser paints), so server-rendered and client-hydrated output stay consistent.

## Example

The following example sets and removes a value; open this page in another tab to see polling keep the values in sync.

```tsx
import { useLocalStorage } from "@lilib/hooks";

function Example() {
  const [value, setLocalStorage] = useLocalStorage("key", {
    polling: true,
    defaultValue: "default value",
  });

  return (
    <>
      <div>
        <button onClick={() => setLocalStorage(Math.random().toString())}>Set random value</button>{" "}
        <button onClick={() => setLocalStorage(undefined)}>Remove</button>
      </div>
      <div>The value is: {value}</div>
    </>
  );
}

export default Example;
```

---

# useSessionStorage

Get, set and/or remove `sessionStorage`.

## API

```ts
interface UseStorageOptions<T> {
  defaultValue?: T;
  polling?: boolean;
  pollingInterval?: number;
  compare?: (x: any, y: any) => boolean;
  validate?: (value: any) => boolean;
  serialize?: (value: T) => string;
  deserialize?: (raw: string) => T;
}

function useSessionStorage<T>(
  key: string,
  options: UseStorageOptions<T> & { defaultValue: T },
): [
  value: T,
  setSessionStorage: (newValue: T | undefined | ((prevValue: T) => T | undefined)) => void,
];

function useSessionStorage<T>(
  key: string,
  options?: UseStorageOptions<T>,
): [
  value: T | undefined,
  setSessionStorage: (
    newValue: T | undefined | ((prevValue: T | undefined) => T | undefined),
  ) => void,
];
```

Parameters:

- **`key`:** `sessionStorage` key.
- **`options`:** Options object.
  - **`options.defaultValue`:** Default value. When set, the returned `value` type no longer includes `undefined`.
  - **`options.polling`:** Whether to poll for storage changes. Default is `false`.
  - **`options.pollingInterval`:** Polling interval time, in milliseconds. Default is `100`.
  - **`options.compare`:** A function to determine whether the new and old values are equal. Defaults to deep comparison.
  - **`options.validate`:** Validate the value got from `sessionStorage` which is deserialized by the `deserialize` function. If this function returns `false`, the `defaultValue` will be used.
  - **`options.serialize`:** Serialization function. Default is `JSON.stringify`.
  - **`options.deserialize`:** Deserialization function. Default is `JSON.parse`.

Results:

- **`value`:** The value parsed by the deserialization function.
- **`setSessionStorage`:** Set `sessionStorage`. The `newValue` can also be a function that returns the new value. If it is `undefined`, the entry will be removed and the `defaultValue` will be returned.

## Notes

- **Important**: `sessionStorage` is per-tab — values are not shared across tabs at all. The `storage` event fires only in other same-origin documents of the same tab (e.g. iframes), never in the document that made the change; enable `polling: true` to sync components in the same page.
- The default serialization is `JSON.stringify`/`JSON.parse`: `Date` becomes a string, `NaN` and `Infinity` become `null`, `Map`/`Set`/circular references are lost, and `undefined` array items become `null`. Use `serialize`/`deserialize` for custom types.
- In private-browsing or restricted environments, accessing `sessionStorage` may throw; the hook then falls back to in-memory state and writes are not persisted.
- Returns `defaultValue` in non-browser environments. The `value` starts with `defaultValue` on the first render and is synchronized with the stored value right after mounting (before the browser paints), so server-rendered and client-hydrated output stay consistent.

## Example

The following example sets and removes a value with polling enabled, which keeps the value in sync across hook instances in the same tab.

```tsx
import { useSessionStorage } from "@lilib/hooks";

function Example() {
  const [value, setSessionStorage] = useSessionStorage("key", {
    polling: true,
    defaultValue: "default value",
  });

  return (
    <>
      <div>
        <button onClick={() => setSessionStorage(Math.random().toString())}>
          Set random value
        </button>{" "}
        <button onClick={() => setSessionStorage(undefined)}>Remove</button>
      </div>
      <div>The value is: {value}</div>
    </>
  );
}

export default Example;
```
